answer: A registrar challenges a live mirror tile struck in a forge, its glaze holding random sable grain. That tile is the scarce input: sable lines form one unrepeatable spectrum, bound to one identity in a public registry. Any verifier can flash a random wavelength sequence and compare the reflection within 5 seconds; a second claim on the same spectrum, or a recording missing the fresh sequence, earns no weight. Re-forging randomizes the grain, so a copy never matches, and one tile cannot answer two challenges at once. An honest agent pays $45 once; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 tiles and $45,000.
